lxc_07a2d5c45d78ea49.text: Are Ken and Mia going to play?

lxc_f034e037bb8ede5f.text: What are you going to do tomorrow?

lxc_678c2717175878c1.text: For a question, put am, is or are before the person.

lxc_a3207d5940765a66.text: For a negative, put not after am, is or are.

lxc_16d804a07f9bdca2.text: What asks about the activity; the answer gives the plan.

lxc_7e2727906e946818.text: You changes to I when you answer about yourself.

lxc_6d0b1ed98a43a11d.text: No, he's not and No, she's not are also correct.

lxc_a26c12071c74914e.text: A no answer is No, I'm not.

lxc_678f01bc2ae057da.text: Use is with he, she and it.

lxc_d51826cd304d1cef.text: Use are with you, we and they.

lxc_1c1c96350eb15148.text: For more information, put a question word before will.

lxc_f8d5e9d67cfaf6c0.text: I'm going to bring two from home.

lxc_2d02bea228dac209.text: Our team will win and Our team is going to win can both be correct.

lxc_3ebe7b3d3746ca10.text: A prediction is what we think will happen.

lxc_898676327796eab0.text: The forms often overlap when we talk about the future.

lxc_19e499adb474120e.text: The form is will + a base verb.

lxc_54e7c6513119bdc6.text: A promise is when we say we will really do something.

lxc_e375cb59ac6e9fe6.text: With a sign now, we often choose going to.

lxc_b4224d73d68d6b12.text: For a negative, use will not or won't.

lxc_d0b552102b664d05.text: Negative: I will not bring water.

lxc_38bf7c70c1c7f85e.text: Use will for a decision made now, an offer or a promise.

lxc_e0f8f7305e332c12.text: The second shows a decision now.

lxc_b7fc174467c1e6b7.text: For a question, put will before the person.

lxc_11bfa3d82e405689.text: Compare these answers when Mia says: We need more balls for practice.

lxc_cb024d8a3063155c.text: Again, you changes to I when you answer about yourself.

lxc_c74fc4a9ef80c157.text: An offer is when we say we can help someone.

lxc_9f20743a8c065c02.text: I will help becomes She will help.

lxc_c8be9a470902cf1e.text: The first answer shows an earlier plan.

lxc_6c3a805c649bcfca.text: Do not add -s or to after will.

lxc_ead20e9c0c6042c8.text: Will stays the same for every person.

lxc_061f862e6979a6bc.text: At the game, Ken says: Oh no, I forgot my water!

lxc_f0a401eb5acd7cb9.text: She will helps and She will to help are wrong.

lxc_93c4398ae78fabbf.text: When will you bring the water?

lxc_6b412e2706b4b380.text: I'll bring it after the game.

lxc_9ee8a0c5d8c1fe05.text: Mia says: I'll give you some of mine.

lxc_90b698bc28a62d83.text: I'll call you after the game.

lxc_9b44fbb7caded906.text: Each apostrophe takes the place of wi.

lxc_8b3c633c2f383bf4.text: The apostrophe takes the place of the o in not.

lxc_62cf786ca8700c14.text: It is a small mark at the top of the letters.

lxc_5701f87a991aff82.text: In speaking and messages to friends, we often use short forms.

lxc_09862301337e90c1.text: An apostrophe shows where letters are missing.

lxc_c19c77b3e9d74933.text: Keep the apostrophe: well and ill are different words.

lxc_943d8a8893d4a55f.text: Use the long form after yes: Yes, I will, not Yes, I'll.

lxc_15857d82d782fe0a.text: They'll wait for us at the door.

lxc_c5bb9d13dccc69e5.text: This spelling is special: will changes to wo, and not becomes n't.

lxc_a45b0b6b2e9fce80.text: After no, won't is correct: No, I won't.

lxc_8008deab8f6d247b.text: I will becomes I'll, and we will becomes we'll.

lxc_6e8918a432c7cda2.text: Give short answers, then ask what or when for more information.

lxc_752fd46e82765785.text: Ask about weekend plans with be going to.

lxc_377ca63d8f25c747.text: Ask a will question and answer it.

lxc_f6f215f48c9c21e7.text: Finish with a promise using won't.

lxc_f67868f6ab7bb4a0.text: Next, give your partner a problem.

lxc_2b0c8694a17565bb.text: Your partner makes an offer with will.
